claim: Use tiny proof programs or learning tests when a model confidently describes behavior that can be checked at runtime.
Keep research, design, structure, and plan documents because they carry decisions into fresh context windows.
Approve a structured outline before allowing a long implementation loop to run.
Make each implementation phase small enough to finish in one context window and place checks at useful boundaries.
A simple plan then implement flow can hide an architectural assumption and produce poor code on a complex change.
Split very large work across several research files, plans, and independently shippable parts.
